prompt:
Edit the supplied approved 4-by-4 Korean hero game sprite sheet into ONE alternate costume sheet. This is a production animation atlas on a truly transparent RGBA background. Preserve the exact hero identity, face, age, hair, beard, equipment, weapon handedness, compact stylized proportions, painterly sculpted 3D illustration finish, soft directional lighting, camera elevation and all 16 poses from the reference. Do not redesign the hero.
Layout: exactly 16 complete full-body actors in 4 columns and 4 rows. Columns left to right: front-right, back-right, back-left, front-left. Rows top to bottom: idle, walk with left foot forward, walk with right foot forward, attack. Back views must really show the back, not mirrored front faces. Preserve the reference's attack type and equipment. A book/command hero keeps an extended commanding hand; an archer draws the same bow; a spear hero thrusts the spear.
Apply the following costume consistently to ALL 16 actors, including the actual back side:
Change the brigandine coat to softly brushed antique gold plates over deep navy cloth; warm ochre seams and muted bronze rivets. Keep the large navy cape with burgundy lining, long crimson plume, bow and quiver. Matte metal highlights, no glowing gold aura.
Keep the same calm muted color grading and convincing cloth/metal/leather as the reference. No scenery, ground, cast shadow, snow, border, text, labels, cell lines or effects. No bloom, aura or detached sparkles. Each actor, including weapon tips, cape, plume, hands, shoes and arrows, must be fully contained within its own cell with generous transparent gutters, at least 28 pixels around it. Never let neighboring actors or their silhouettes touch or overlap. Keep one consistent actor scale for the entire sheet; reduce to fit if necessary. Keep a transparent outer border on all four sides. Preserve transparency, not a checkerboard or colored background.
